verification.fact_verification_explanation: The customer's central allegation is that the 60-days-past-due credit report entry is wrong because they never missed a payment in 18 months. The records contradict this. The transaction history shows the 2026-03-18 and 2026-04-18 scheduled installments of $140.00 each were not received. On 2026-04-20 the account was reported to the credit bureaus as 60 days past due, two days after the second missed installment. The customer later paid $280.00 on 2026-05-18, covering both missed installments, and the 2026-06-18 installment of $140.00 was received on time. The account is now current. The delinquency report did happen, but the customer's explanation, that no payments were missed, is wrong. The customer's bank statements are not on file, but the company's own payment ledger would hold any payment received, so the missing statements do not change the finding. The history only shows payments in Jan-Feb 2026 and from May 2026 on, so the customer's claim about earlier months cannot be checked, but it does not affect the dispute over the March and April installments. Drafting note: the records show two missed installments at the time of reporting, but the oldest unpaid installment (2026-03-18) was about 33 days old on 2026-04-20. A human reviewer may want to confirm how the '60 days past due' label was derived before the response states the reporting was accurate.
verification.risk_rationale: There is no attorney/regulator reference, no identity-theft dispute, no claim of being misled about loan terms, no hardship or vulnerability indicators, and no embedded instructions. The missed installments are $140 each, and the claim is confirmed false against clear payment records.

policy.text:
# Policy: Credit Reporting Disputes (Fair Credit Reporting Act)

**Applies to:** Any complaint alleging inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable information reported to a consumer reporting agency (credit bureau).

## Requirements
- As a furnisher of information, we must investigate a dispute (received either directly from the consumer or relayed by a credit bureau) within **30 days**, extendable to **45 days** if the consumer provides additional information during the 30-day window.
- We must review all relevant information provided by the consumer, correct any inaccuracy found, and report the results of the investigation back to the consumer and, if applicable, to the credit bureau.
- If an item is found to be inaccurate or unverifiable, it must be corrected or deleted from our reporting **promptly**.
- We may not resume reporting an item we previously deleted unless we can certify the information is accurate and complete.
- A consumer may request a statement of the dispute to be included in their credit file if the dispute is not resolved to their satisfaction.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May confirm whether our internal records match or contradict what is reported (e.g., payment history, account status).
- May state the applicable 30/45-day investigation timeline.
- May NOT promise a specific bureau will update within a specific number of days — we control our own furnishing, not the bureau's processing timeline.

## Escalation trigger
A **third or subsequent dispute on the same item**, or any complaint stating an investigation was closed with no explanation of what was actually checked, should be escalated — repeated unresolved disputes carry elevated regulatory risk.

## Remedy authority
Front-line staff may initiate a correction to our own furnished data (status, balance, payment history) when the internal transaction record clearly supports the correction. Removing an account entirely, or correcting identity-mismatch issues, requires supervisor or fraud-team review.

*Source: Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1681 et seq. Generic, illustrative summary for internal training/demo purposes, not legal advice.*

draft.draft_text:
Thank you for reaching out about the 60-days-past-due status showing on your credit report. We understand how concerning it is to see that when you believe you've paid on time every month, so we've looked closely at your payment history.

The past-due status: The account was reported to the credit bureaus as 60 days past due on April 20, 2026. That report came after your $140.00 installments due on March 18 and April 18, 2026 didn't come in to us. On May 18, 2026 we received $280.00, which covered both of those installments, and your June 18 installment of $140.00 arrived on time. Your account is now current.

Your statement that you never missed a payment: For March and April 2026, our payment records don't show those two installments being received, so we can't match them to what you've described. The payment history we reviewed shows payments in January and February 2026 and then from May 2026 onward, so we can't compare it against the earlier months you mention.

Your bank statements: We don't have your bank statements. If they show payments to us on or around March 18 or April 18, 2026, please send them and we'll review them. You're also welcome to send anything else you'd like us to look at.

Where things stand: So far we haven't made any change to how the account is reported. Credit reporting complaints are reviewed within 30 days, and that can extend to 45 days if you send us additional information during that time. If you aren't satisfied with the outcome, you can ask us to include a statement of your dispute in your credit file. We can't say when a credit bureau will update its records, because that is up to the bureau.

You can reply to this message at any time with more information, and we'll review it. Case reference: 23623033.

verifier.completeness_check: pass — all three allegations are addressed: the 60-days-past-due reporting, the claim of never missing a payment, and the bank statements showing on-time payments for 18 months.
verifier.groundedness_check: fail — The draft says: "The account was reported to the credit bureaus as 60 days past due on April 20, 2026. That report came after your $140.00 installments due on March 18 and April 18, 2026 didn't come in to us." This presents the missed installments as the basis for the 60-day label. The verification output says the oldest unpaid installment (March 18) was only about 33 days old on April 20, and tells the reviewer to confirm how the '60 days past due' label was derived before the response implies the reporting was accurate. That discrepancy is unresolved, and the draft does not flag it or hedge. All other dates and amounts ($140.00 installments, $280.00 on May 18, the June 18 installment, account now current, no statements on file) trace to the verification output.
verifier.policy_authorization_check: pass — No remedy or referral is stated (remedy_stated and referral_stated are null). The draft says no change has been made to reporting and promises no correction, deletion, or approval. The 30/45-day timeline and statement-of-dispute language match Policy 04.
verifier.prohibited_language_check: pass — The draft has no fault admission, no guarantee about the future, no legal conclusion, and nothing discouraging other channels. "We can't say when a credit bureau will update its records" is consistent with the policy limit on bureau timing promises.
verifier.tone_structure_check: pass — The draft follows the required order: acknowledgment tied to the specific complaint, findings in separate paragraphs per allegation, a status/outcome paragraph, next steps, and the case reference (23623033). The tone is plain and professional, and the length is acceptable for a multi-allegation response. The outcome paragraph is thin ("So far we haven't made any change") but acceptable as a pending-status statement.
specific_issues: Groundedness: the draft implies that the two missed installments account for the '60 days past due' reporting, even though the verification output flags that the oldest unpaid installment was only about 33 days old at the time of reporting. The draft should either avoid linking the 60-day label to the missed installments until a human confirms how it was derived, or be flagged for reviewer confirmation before sending.

draft.draft_text:
Thank you for writing to us about the 60 days past due mark on your credit report. You told us you've never missed a payment on this account and that your bank statements show every payment went through on time for the past 18 months. Seeing a late mark you believe is wrong is worrying, and we understand why you wanted it looked at.

Here is what we found, point by point.

The 60 days past due entry: Our records show that on April 20, 2026, the account was reported to the credit bureaus as 60 days past due. We're having that 60-day label checked against the payment dates on your account, so we can confirm how it was worked out.

Never missing a payment: Our payment records show that the $140.00 installments due on March 18, 2026 and April 18, 2026 were not received. On May 18, 2026, we received a payment of $280.00, which covers both of those amounts. The $140.00 installment due June 18, 2026 was received on time, and our records show your account is current.

Your bank statements and the past 18 months: We don't have your bank statements on file. The payment history we reviewed shows payments in January and February 2026 and from May 2026 onward, so we couldn't check the months before January 2026. If your statements show payments leaving your account around March 18 or April 18, 2026, please send them to us. We'll review them.

Outcome: Based on our payment records, we haven't found a payment that changes what we have on file for March and April 2026, so no correction has been made at this point. The check on the 60-day label is still under way.

Next steps: Under our process for credit reporting disputes, we review the dispute within 30 days. That can be extended to 45 days if you send us additional information during that time. You're welcome to send us anything else at any time, and we'll review it. If you're not satisfied with the result, you can ask for a statement of your dispute to be included in your credit file. You're also free to contact any other organization about this if you choose to.

Case reference: 23623033
